subject: Head-to-head engine slate — summary & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@clarify.ai>, Darren Liu <darren@clarify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Head-to-head engine slate — summary & next steps

Hi Ellie / Darren —

Thanks again for the demo today — really helpful to see the end-to-end flow and the latency constraints you care about for live chat (95th p90 target ~1200ms). Per our conversation I pulled together a short head-to-head shortlist and next steps so we can land on a candidate set to validate with your prompt set. High level takeaways first: 

- Recommendation: run a short 3-model pilot (rwd-small-int8, rwd-medium-q4f16, rwd-large-fp16) to validate quality vs your NPS-like rubric and measure 95/99 latency at your expected concurrency.
- Tradeoffs: small-int8 gives best cost (∼0.12 USD/1k tokens) and lowest median latency; medium-q4f16 is the best quality/cost midpoint; large-fp16 gives highest quality but will need dedicated capacity to keep p99 latency under 2s.
- Immediate asks: access to your 500-message prompt set (we already have the recording + high-level rubric) and permission to run the 48-hour benchmark run on a representative traffic replay.

Attached: headtohead-benchmarks.xlsx (summary), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample), demo recording link. Full benchmark artifacts uploaded here: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/clarify-headtohead-20270612

Suggested next steps:
1) You share the prompt set (or confirm the sample attached covers the primary flows) — Ellie (ETA: Tue 6/15)
2) We run the 48-hour replay on the three candidates, capture cost/latency/error profiles & qualitative diffs (ETA: 6/16–6/18)
3) Joint review: short readout + decision on pilot candidate and rollout plan (6/19 30–45m)

If that timeline works I’ll schedule the benchmark window and a joint review slot — Ben and Marissa are copied to help with run specifics and pricing guidance.

Best,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Ellie Park <ellie@clarify.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Darren Liu <darren@clarify.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Head-to-head engine slate — summary & next steps

Thanks Soojin — this looks good and the timeline is tight but doable. A couple of clarifying Qs before we hand over the full set: 

1) For the medium-q4f16 model, what's the expected cost delta vs small-int8 at our traffic profile (roughly 300 concurrent users, mean prompt 220 tokens, mean response 160 tokens)?
2) We have a compliance requirement to retain full request logs for 90 days; would the pilot require any changes to the way you stream or store KV cache data?

We’ll send the full 500-message prompt set by EOD Monday (6/15). Also: Darren asked whether we can limit the 48-hour run to business hours only (8am–6pm PT) to avoid skew from night traffic.

—Ellie

On Jun 12, 2027, at 3:12 PM, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo today...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@clarify.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Head-to-head engine slate — summary & next steps

Hey Ellie — quick answers to your questions: 

1) Cost delta: rough back-of-envelope for your traffic (300 concurrent, avg interaction ~380 tokens total) — small-int8 ≈ $0.12 / 1k tokens, medium-q4f16 ≈ $0.37 / 1k tokens, large-fp16 ≈ $1.05 / 1k tokens. For a 30-day pilot at your concurrency (business hours only) expect approximate token spend of $2.2k (small), $6.8k (medium), $19.2k (large). I'll post the detailed cost model into the shared benchmark sheet under the "Cost Scenarios" tab.

2) Compliance / logs: the pilot itself doesn't change streaming behavior. For 90-day retention we recommend routing logs to your S3 bucket via our Private Logs connector (no PII is stored by default). Ben / Marissa can walk through minimal config; we just need access to a destination S3 (or you can use our managed retention add-on). For the KV cache: nothing required — KV cache is kept ephemeral and never written to persistent object storage in the default setup. If you need encrypted persistent caches we can enable a customer-managed KMS in Private deployment flows.

We can scope the replay to business hours only — that will still give us a representative latency/cost profile without night skew.

FWIW on quality: we expect medium-q4f16 to close ~60–80% of the gap to the large-fp16 on your rubric for multi-turn coherence and hallucination; small-int8 will be noticeably weaker on long-context summarization but often acceptable for FAQ-style responses. We'll flag any systematic regression in the quality matrix.

I'll update the shared sheet and stand up the runs as soon as we get the prompt set.

Cheers,
Ben

--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-14T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Head-to-head engine slate — summary & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming business-hours-only. Next actions I’ll take after we receive your full prompt set (ETA Mon 6/15):

- Set up the replay job (business-hours-only window). We’ll capture: median/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, per-flow quality scores (your rubric), token-level error rate, and a short sample of qualitative diffs.
- Run configuration: 3 candidates (rwd-small-int8, rwd-medium-q4f16, rwd-large-fp16). Each candidate will be run on identical hardware profiles; large-fp16 will be placed on a provisioned instance to keep tail latency predictable.
- Deliverables (deliver by 6/19):
  * benchmark workbook (xlsx) with cost/latency sheets and per-prompt breakdown
  * prompt-level quality annotation (csv) for the 250 highest-risk prompts
  * a short decision memo with recommended pilot candidate and expected monthly run-rate at production scale

Note on regressions: we’ll implement prompt-level regression detection for hallucination and repetition. If the medium-q4f16 shows a >12% drop vs large-fp16 on your hallucination metric we’ll flag it as a blocker for pilot. The small-int8 will have a softer quality bar and is recommended only if cost reduction is the primary objective.

I’ll schedule the joint readout for 6/19 10:00–10:45 PT unless you prefer a different slot. Ben / Marissa will follow up with the cost appendix and internal run checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Soojin
